resources.label: Cash and equivalents
resources.detail: Cash excludes 46M restricted cash. Cash located at Parent and amounts transferable from each subsidiary are Unavailable.

resources.label: Corporate revolver
resources.detail: General corporate purposes, including permitted acquisitions and restricted payments (§9.13). Borrowing conditions and distribution restrictions still apply.

resources.label: Commodity-linked facility
resources.detail: Supports commodity collateral, working capital and general corporate purposes. Weekly hedge-based borrowing base can fall and require repayment. June capacity is not a later commitment to lend that amount.

resources.label: Receivables facility
resources.detail: Purchase limit rose to 1.25B on July 10, due July 9, 2027. June borrowings 300M. Eligible receivables, advance conditions and a contemporaneous drawing balance are needed; 1.25B less June borrowings is not drawable capacity.

resources.label: Repurchase facility
resources.detail: 125M uncommitted program, extended to July 9, 2027. Secured by the receivables program’s subordinated note. June drawings were zero; no guaranteed cash availability or independent collateral pool is established.

resources.label: BCOP facilities
resources.detail: Zero unused capacity in the June table. Project assets and cash flows service project debt; Pulaski bridge has a Vistra guarantee. The rest is otherwise non-recourse to Vistra Operations and its other subsidiaries.

resources.label: Vistra Zero term loan
resources.detail: Zero unused capacity in the June table; 697M is already drawn and included in debt. Subsidiary guarantees and project security; otherwise non-recourse to Vistra Operations and its other subsidiaries.

resources.label: Texas Energy Fund loan
resources.detail: June table shows 172M drawn and zero unused capacity. The broader 583M development agreement does not establish freely drawable funds. Project use, security and conditions apply; otherwise non-recourse to Vistra Operations and its other subsidiaries.

terms.name: Corporate revolver draw conditions
terms.location: Ex.10.1, clean agreement Annex B §§7.1–7.2, 9.13, 10.9; Compliance Period definition
terms.detail: Each drawing requires no continuing default, specified representations to remain true and a borrowing notice. The springing covenant caps contract-defined total net leverage at 5.50x during a Compliance Period. The trigger exceeds 35% of revolving commitments, with specified LC exclusions including undrawn LCs. Ordinary undrawn LCs reduce availability but are not automatically covenant-trigger usage. Covenant headroom is Unavailable.

terms.name: Commodity-linked borrowing conditions
terms.detail: September amendment retains 1.75B commitments and extends maturity to September 29, 2027. Draws remain subject to the borrowing base, no default, representations and notice. The agreement has a springing contract-defined 5.50x total net leverage covenant for a Compliance Quarter. Current borrowing base, drawings and headroom are Unavailable; June availability is not rolled forward.

terms.name: Receivables and repurchase renewals
terms.location: Ex.4.1 §§2.1–2.5 and Schedule VI; Ex.10.1 §2; 10-Q Note 12 p.27
terms.detail: Receivables amendment extends termination to July 9, 2027 and its purchaser schedule totals 1.25B. RecCo funds purchased eligible receivables under conditions. The separate repo remains uncommitted and uses the subordinated note from that same receivables structure. Capacity and term extensions are not cash receipts.

terms.name: Project repayment and recourse
terms.detail: BCOP term loans amortize over 20 years from conversion using project cash flows. Pulaski construction conversion requires commercial operation and other conditions; the 206M combined term balance has a December 2029 final maturity, not a single 206M balloon established here. Vistra guarantees the 261M bridge. Vistra Zero and Permian obligations have separate security and recourse terms. Project cash available for parent obligations is Unavailable.

terms.name: Parent distributions
terms.location: 10-K Note 13 p.116; Schedule I pp.159–160; 10-Q Note 12 p.23
terms.detail: At December 31, 2025 the annual filing said Vistra Operations restricted net assets could be distributed to Parent, and reported 1.625B of subsidiary dividends received during 2025. That does not locate June cash or establish a future parent distribution. The June filing describes investment and dividend restrictions that can apply following a downgrade below investment grade. No future transfer amount is assumed.

limits: June 30 is the cash and availability date. Current cash, drawable capacity, parent-accessible cash and contractual covenant headroom are Unavailable.
Operating cash flow is seasonal and weighted toward the second half. The first-half result and TTM figures do not establish future recurring cash generation.
Interest cash in operating cash flow is not deducted twice. Nuveen principal paid in financing is separate from interest paid in operating cash flow.

Posted margin deposits of 1.436B and affiliate-financed eligible assets of 438M are already posted, not additional cash sources. Trust-security sale proceeds are reinvested within nuclear decommissioning funds and do not represent gross free cash available for debt repayment.

Letters of credit total 3.587B: 1.092B corporate revolver, 1.759B other LOC facilities and 736M alternative facilities. The 1.092B already reduces revolver availability. Other LOC facilities are uncommitted credit support, not extra cash borrowing capacity.

Note 12 also states 13M of BCOP debt-service reserve LCs while its credit facilities table displays zero project LCs. Scope/overlap with the 3.587B total is not established; no additional aggregate is inferred.

The 2025 annual maturity schedule is historical. First-half refinancing and new debt prevent carrying it forward as remaining June maturities. The selected dated payments are not a full debt-service or obligations schedule.

Cogentrix expected cash consideration is approximately 2.3B, with an estimated 1.5B of debt assumed and 5M shares also contemplated. Closing conditions and adjustments apply; late-2026 closing was an expectation, not a confirmed payment date or completed transaction.

Helix initial 500M remains callable at June 30. Funded-to-date and call dates are Unavailable. The additional 500M milestones had not occurred; Vistra could elect to invest anyway. Neither amount is scheduled into December.

No forecast surplus, cash runway or overall repayment shortfall is calculated. Future collateral calls, capex, acquisitions and transfer restrictions prevent combining dated cash and capacity into a promised funding result.

events.finding: Corporate revolving credit commitments increased from $3.44 billion to $5.50 billion and certain guarantees and covenants changed. The event preceded the June 30 balance sheet; $5.50 billion is facility capacity, not an additional borrowing after that date.

Receivables purchasers' aggregate commitment rose from $1.1 billion to $1.25 billion, and the agreement was extended to July 9, 2027. The separate repurchase facility was also extended to that date. The $1.25 billion is capacity, not a reported outstanding borrowing.
Reports PJM electricity capacity auction results for planning year 2028/2029; it does not report a new borrowing or financing facility.

Exhibit 99.1 reports June 30 liquidity, including $4,408 million corporate revolver availability and $1,452 million commodity-linked availability. These are June 30 availability figures, not later borrowing. The release also discusses the Helix investment commitment, which is outside baseline debt.
Registers securities for possible offerings. The later pricing sheet, final prospectus and September 24 8-K identify the completed junior-note issuance; this registration is not a separate borrowing.

Preliminary prospectus for the two junior-note series due 2057 has blank principal amounts and rates. The later FWP supplies pricing and the September 24 8-K confirms issuance; this document is not another borrowing.

events.kind: Pricing terms; same notes as September 24 issuance
events.finding: Pricing sheet for $850 million Series A and $650 million Series B junior subordinated notes due 2057, with initial rates of 7.000% and 7.250%. It projected September 24 settlement; the later 8-K confirms issuance. This is not additional debt beyond that issuance.

events.kind: Final offering terms; same notes as September 24 issuance
events.finding: Final prospectus estimates about $1.48 billion in net proceeds. It says proceeds are intended for general corporate purposes, including possible redemption of Series A and B preferred stock at or after their October and December reset dates. Redemption is not confirmed here; the prospectus is not another issuance.

events.kind: New debt issued after balance sheet
events.finding: Vistra Operations completed $1.5 billion of junior subordinated notes due 2057: $850 million Series A at an initial 7.000% and $650 million Series B at an initial 7.250%, guaranteed by Vistra. The indenture permits interest deferral for up to 10 consecutive years per period, subject to its terms. This issuance is not part of June 30 debt.
Commodity-linked revolving credit facility maturity was extended from September 30, 2026 to September 29, 2027. This filing does not establish an additional amount borrowed.
